newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Schmidhuber says EMU can start in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Schmidhuber says EMU can start in 1999.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Peter Schmidhuber on Tuesday said the planned 1999 start date for the single European currency was realistic and urged strict adherence to entry criteria for the launch.

"If there is strict compliance with convergence criteria at the start of the third stage of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), and member states set a firm lasting budget policy ... the start of Stage 3 in 1999 is possible," he said.
Schmidhuber made the comments in a speech prepared for delivery to the American Chamber of Commerce in Munich. A copy was made available in advance.
Schmidhuber said there was no reason at present to question the start date for EMU.
"That would only lead to further uncertainty and thus endanger the whole timetable," he said.
Schmidhuber said entry criteria set down in the Maastricht Treaty for taking part in the EMU launch had to be observed.
"The government and the Bundesbank is of the opinion that these criteria must be kept strictly," he said.

Rumours have circulated in recent weeks that Germany was softening its stance on strict adherence to EMU convergence criteria, which include targets for countries' budget deficits at or below three percent of gross domestic product and debt at or below 60 percent of GDP.
Bonn and the Bundesbank have dismissed the speculation.
Schmidhuber said efforts at budgetary consolidation by member states were essential both to meet Maastricht entry criteria and to secure longer term economic growth and efficiency.
